script: Am I the jerk for taking my brother off my insurance after warning him three times?. I had my brother on my auto policy since he moved back to our city because his own quote was almost triple mine. His share was $310 a month, and he was supposed to send it the same day my payment came out. He paid on time for five months, then it got messy—texts on the 3rd, the 9th, half of it, then the rest whenever. but here's the thing… In February I told him if he fell two months behind I'd take him off at renewal. I repeated that in March, and in April I sent him the actual renewal date, saying, "this is the last time I am going to bring it up." He said he was good for it and I was being dramatic about family. but here's the thing… Renewal came, the $740 was still outstanding, and I removed him. I texted him the day it processed so there'd be no confusion about when coverage ended. He kept driving like it didn't matter. and that's when everything changed… Two weeks later he got pulled over for a taillight and cited for no insurance. Now there's a court date, a suspension he's fighting, and he told Mom I did it behind his back to teach him a lesson. Mom says I was right but should have called instead of texting because he doesn't read texts, and that I knew that about him. what I didn't know was that the whole thing would become a legal battle. I do know that about him. I still think three warnings is three warnings. If this didn't work, I'd lose everything—my peace, my patience, my sanity. This wasn't just about money; it was about respect, responsibility, and the fact that family should act like adults. but here's the thing… So yeah, I was the jerk or not, I stood my ground, and that's the tea.
